source_text: Quid est quod laboras magnis argumentationibus pervenire ad impietatis abruptum, ut "Christi caro, quia de Maria natus est, cuius virginis caro sicut ceterorum omnium ex Adam fuerat propagata, nihil distet a carne peccati, et sine ulla distinctione Apostolus dixisse credatur, eum fuisse missum in similitudine carnis peccati [n125] "; immo potius instas, "ut nulla sit caro peccati, ne hoc sit et Christi"? … Sed "hanc apostolicam sententiam me non intellexisse" dixisti
pass_a_gloss: What is it that you labour with great argumentations to arrive at the precipice of impiety, that 'the flesh of Christ, because he was born of Mary, whose virgin flesh like that of all the others had been propagated from Adam, differs nothing from the flesh of sin, and without any distinction the Apostle is believed to have said that he was sent in the likeness of the flesh of sin'; nay rather you insist 'that there be no flesh of sin, lest this be also Christ's'? But 'that I had not understood this apostolic sentence' you said.
pass_b_english: Augustine reports, speaking to Julian: “Why do you labor with great arguments to reach the brink of impiety, so that ‘the flesh of Christ, because he was born of Mary, whose virgin flesh had been propagated from Adam like that of everyone else, differs in no way from sinful flesh, and the Apostle is believed to have said without any distinction that he was sent in the likeness of sinful flesh’ (Romans 8:3)? Or rather you press the point ‘that no flesh is sinful flesh, so that Christ’s may not be so either.’”
“But you said ‘that I had not understood this saying of the Apostle.’”

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.

choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-d): the old English summarised Augustine's report ('Augustine reports that Julian ...') instead of translating it. Now a translation of the Latin clause(s) that carry Julian's words or Augustine's report of them, with Augustine named as speaker where the words are his; nothing added that the Latin does not say. Omitted stretches inside a paragraph are marked with an ellipsis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.
